doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

chapter: Improvisation and the Creative Music Studio
title: Not seeing themselves as history; Savia; marketing the music
summary: She just does what she does, appreciates audience response, mentions daughter Savia, and the music is hard to market.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Wow. This is sometimes a hard question. Did you and Karl feel like over the years you were doing something that was an important part of jazz history?
Maybe Karl but I never, no. I just do what I do.
You just do what you are doing.

And when people appreciate it I am honored. I love it. I’m happy. It makes my day. Even if it’s only one person coming up, but usually it’s many. You know some people come up and say, “I felt so shitty” you know, “and now I feel so good.”
How did your daughters feel about what you —
Savia. She’s a dancer and so definitely she has incredible feeling for rhythm and music.
How is this music, it’s obviously a challenge to market it.
